name: uri-host-hex-suffix-label-invalid
description: permittedSubtrees uniformResourceIdentifier is 'example.com'. The leaf's URI SAN is 'foo://example.com.0xca/path' — a host whose last label is a hex literal ('0xca'). The trailing label looks like a hostname component but inet_pton-style resolvers may parse it as the high byte of an IPv4 address (a hex form once accepted by glibc and BSD libc). RFC 5280 §4.2.1.10 says iPAddress is a separate GeneralName type — a URI whose host parses as an IP must be rejected as malformed against a URI constraint. BoringSSL's recent URI hardening explicitly rejects this shape; older OpenSSL-family parsers may treat the trailing '.0xca' as a DNS label and suffix-match 'example.com' against the leftmost portion, incorrectly accepting.
references: BoringSSL b84dc606 — crypto/x509: Tighten URI name constraints parsing and matching
notes: Companion to uri-hex-ipv4-host-invalid (all-hex labels). This case is sneakier — only the LAST label is hex-shaped, so a parser that only checks leftmost or all-labels may miss it. The hex-suffix attack relies on inet_aton's historical tolerance of mixed-radix dotted forms, where a final hex value is treated as the low octets of the address.
